answer: Cuckoo-rule committee shuffling stops sybils from pooling. Each epoch a ledger beacon maps agents onto a ring split into 64 grading committees. When a newcomer joins at a random point, the four agents nearest it get evicted to fresh random spots, so no cluster stays put. Each committee then grades only its own answers. An attacker can't wander in and pile up; in a 9,000-agent network he needs about 3,000 bots, and at a 25 POA bond each that is 75,000 POA locked. Small farms come out hollow, like planting saplings in an orchard where a gardener replants random trees each night.
